items.a: A lightbox sign is an illuminated sign housed in an aluminum cabinet with a translucent printed face — vinyl or acrylic — lit from behind by internal LEDs.

items.q: Cabinet signs vs channel letters — what's the difference?
items.a: Channel letters are individually fabricated 3D letters. Cabinet signs are enclosed boxes with a single printed face. Cabinets are typically faster and more cost-effective, and their faces are easier to refresh.

items.q: How much does an illuminated lightbox sign cost?
items.a: Typical projects range $2,000 to $10,000. Large custom cabinets or pylon mounts can exceed $20,000 depending on size and structural requirements.

items.q: Can you print my logo and colors on the face?
items.a: Yes. We print full-color weather-rated vinyl or direct-print acrylic faces. Pantone matching is standard.

items.q: How long do LED lightbox signs last?
items.a: The aluminum cabinet and LED system last 10 to 15 years (LEDs rated for 50,000+ hours). Printed faces typically need refresh every 5 to 8 years depending on sun exposure.
Single-sided mounts flush against a wall and is visible from one direction. Double-sided projects perpendicular from the building as a blade sign, visible from both street directions.

items.q: Can cabinet faces be replaced without rewiring?
items.a: Yes. Cabinet face panels are designed to swap independently from the LED and wiring system — useful for rebrands or rotating promotions.

items.q: How much power does a lightbox consume?
items.a: Modern LED cabinets draw roughly 50 to 150 watts for a 4×3 ft storefront sign — comparable to a few household bulbs.

items.q: Are lightbox signs weather-rated for Chicago?
items.a: Yes. Sealed aluminum cabinets, weather-rated LEDs, and UV-stabilized faces handle the full Midwest temperature and precipitation range.

items.q: Do you handle permits for illuminated signs?
items.a: Yes. We file both sign and electrical permits with the Village. Typical turnaround is 2 to 4 weeks, running in parallel with fabrication.
Standard cabinets range from 2×2 feet up to 10×8 feet. Larger installations are fabricated modular and joined on site.

items.q: Can you build a multi-tenant cabinet for a plaza?
items.a: Yes. We build shared cabinet frameworks with replaceable per-tenant panels — a common solution for strip malls and multi-tenant buildings.
